what:
Binary migration — DO NOT unpublish `aide-memory@0.1.1` until the binary is verified end-to-end (user decision 2026-04-20).

Sequencing rule:
1. Publish binary as `aide-memory@0.2.0` (npm wrapper) ALONGSIDE 0.1.1 — parallel, not replacement
2. Soak period: minimum 14 days + ≥20 real users + zero P0 bugs (user to confirm exact thresholds)
3. Only AFTER soak passes: deprecate or unpublish 0.1.1. PREFER `npm deprecate` over `npm unpublish` unless npm policy forces unpublish — deprecate leaves the version resolvable for anyone pinned, but warns on install.

This invalidates the "Phase 0 — unpublish v0.1.1" task in the pre-existing `docs/specs/BINARY_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` (on `feature/phase-1`). That phase is REPLACED by:
- Phase 0: baseline + branch (keep)
- Phase 7: soft launch (publish 0.2.0 alongside 0.1.1)
- Phase 8: soak period (burn-in with exit criteria)
- Phase 9: verified unpublish/deprecate (only after 7+8 pass)

v0.1.1 is the rollback safety net. Unpublishing before verification = no rollback path for early-binary users who hit platform-specific bugs.
why: No-unpublish-until-verified rule is now baked into the plan at §4.1 and Phases 7-9. Demoting to normal — plan carries the canonical version.
